current_flow: gl-month-rollups adds two READ-ONLY warehouse views mirroring actual_by_key_month: actual_by_gl_month reduces DUB actuals to (gl_code, month) over cost centres (constant plant='DUB' column, active-batch filter inherited), and budget_by_gl_month rolls the active budget batch to (gl_code, month) via its own ingest_batch join, preserving a deterministic Budget-Components label set and carrying raw rollover with no measure. Both are drizzle pgViews + a journalled 0002 migration; hermetic SQL-shape tests; and a WAREHOUSE_DB_TEST=1 gated proof that uses IngestionRepository (prior-then-replacement, both sides) to prove each rollup reflects only the active batch, serialized with the existing reconciliation proof in test:warehouse-proof. No endpoint, grant, base table, or dependency; no cross-object join (task 2).
new_abstractions: actual_by_gl_month (DUB actual reduction to gl_code+month, constant plant column, inherited active-batch lineage)
budget_by_gl_month (active budget rollup to gl_code+month with a deterministic Budget-Components label set)
a serialized test:warehouse-proof running both this and the reconciliation gated proof (shared-table truncation)

criteria_map.a demonstrated warehouse-DB test proves: KEEP (amended). The gated proof uses IngestionRepository to load PRIOR then REPLACEMENT batches for BOTH actuals and budget, asserting the prior stays inactive and only the active batch contributes - proving the candidate-load-then-flip invariant, not just a static seed.

gaps: The host-verification commands do not exist from repo root: `npm run warehouse:migrate` and `test:warehouse-proof` are backend workspace scripts, so the D-0008 proof would never run as written.

The migration was not a complete owned artifact: drizzle applies only migrations declared in backend/drizzle-warehouse/meta/_journal.json, which the contract did not own, so a clean warehouse could not be relied on to apply the new views.

Criterion C3 did not actually require proving INACTIVE Actual exclusion: the test seeded multi-cost-centre active actuals but a retained prior batch only for Budget, and direct SQL seeding would not prove the atomic candidate-load-then-flip active-batch invariant.

Proof registration was underspecified and risked failing quality-gate or dropping the existing reconciliation proof: every backend *.test.ts must be in exactly one declared suite, and the current test:warehouse-proof runs only reconciliation.repository.test.ts; both destructive proofs truncate shared warehouse tables.
array_agg(DISTINCT cost_center) is not deterministic without ORDER BY, but the story requires a deterministic label set for provenance and golden fixtures.

The Actual rollup drops plant, yet the dependent task 2 is contracted to inject an Actual-side plant scope predicate inside its source CTE - the seam was undecided, forcing task 2 to violate its RBAC contract or recompute the rollup.

The hermetic-test instruction was internally ambiguous: it asked BOTH views to assert an active-batch filter, but actual_by_gl_month INHERITS that filter through actual_by_key_month and has no direct ingest_batch predicate.
resolutions: Pin backend-workspace-prefixed commands: `npm --prefix backend run warehouse:migrate` and `npm --prefix backend run test:warehouse-proof`, retaining the TS_NODE_PROJECT/ts-node prefix required by decision 0009.
Added backend/drizzle-warehouse/meta/_journal.json to write_scope; the task owns BOTH the new 0002_gl_month_rollups.sql and its journal entry so a clean warehouse applies the views.

The gated proof uses IngestionRepository (not direct SQL) to load a PRIOR then a REPLACEMENT actuals batch (and budget), asserting the prior stays inactive, only the replacement/active batch contributes, and the rollup sums the replacement's cost centres to one row - proving the candidate-load-then-flip invariant for BOTH sides.

Add gl-month-rollups.db.test.ts to test:hermetic + its hermeticTests registry in quality-gate (exactly one suite; gated leaf self-skips), and EXTEND test:warehouse-proof to run BOTH this and reconciliation.repository.test.ts SERIALIZED (--test-concurrency=1), so neither destructive proof wipes the other mid-run.
Use array_agg(DISTINCT cost_center ORDER BY cost_center) for a deterministic informational label set, and assert the order in the tests.
HUMAN-decided (round): EXPOSE a constant plant='DUB' column in actual_by_gl_month so task 2 injects/verifies its Actual-side scope predicate against the rollup - a visible, testable RBAC seam.

actual_by_gl_month's test proves the INHERITED active-batch lineage (via actual_by_key_month) plus the DUB reduction (no direct ingest_batch predicate - do not duplicate the join), while budget_by_gl_month's test proves its DIRECT active-batch join.
